gaps.issue: The headline is false as worded. README title, README paragraph 1 and RESULTS paragraph 1 say 584 of 593 changes 'arrived on the next NYSE session date'. The metric behind 584 counts NYSE sessions elapsed through the posting date. Two changes were posted on Saturdays one day after the next session: the 2024-08-01 label at 2024-08-03 09:09:23 ET and the 2024-10-31 label at 2024-11-02 09:09:35 ET. Recomputed from the replay, 582 of 593 were posted on the next NYSE session date. The NYSE calendar also hides a stronger answer. Six of the nine NYSE exceptions are Columbus Day and Veterans Day in 2024, 2025 and 2026, when Superstate's own labels carry the prior NAV, so the fund did not value. Against Superstate's own valuation dates (spell starts, using labels up to the official NAV date), 589 of 593 changes posted on the next valuation date. Four were one day late (2024-08-01, 2024-08-27, 2024-10-31, 2026-10-30), and 8 values never appeared.
gaps.fix: In ustb_metrics.analyze, add two per-change fields: posted_on_next_nyse_session_date (ET posting date equals the first NYSE session after the label) and posted_on_next_valuation_date (ET posting date equals the next issuer spell start after the label). Summarize both. Lead the README and RESULTS with the valuation-date count, for example: '589 of 593 changed USTB NAVs reached Chainlink's Ethereum feed on Superstate's next valuation date. 4 were a day late and 8 never appeared.' Keep 582/593 (NYSE date) and 584/593 (within one NYSE session) as secondary rows with their exact definitions. Name the four late cases and the bond-market-holiday carries in RESULTS.

gaps.issue: The final labels in scope are API forward fills, not NAV observations. In the pinned capture (fetched 2026-11-27 04:00 UTC), the 11/25, 11/26 and 11/27 labels all equal the 11/24 NAV 11.291441, and financials official.nav_date is 2026-11-24. A reviewer read at 04:27 UTC with end_date=2026-11-28 returned a 11/28 label with the same value, which is a future date. November 25 was a normal valuation day. Its published NAV will replace the fill. The study counts both filled days as data: 1,059 labels to November 26, 883 comparison dates, 426 window labels, daily rows for 2026-11-25 and 2026-11-26 at 0 bp (the two dots on the zero line at the right edge of the chart), and the pinned USTB live window for November 20 to 26. SOURCES 'Capture boundary' describes the 11/25 and 11/26 values as retained labels, not as provisional fills.
gaps.fix: In feed_history.replay, cap label-dependent metrics at min(block UTC date - 1, financials.official.nav_date). Drop or flag 'provisional' the daily rows after the official date. Recompute labels_sha256 and the ustb-capture.json reference, update every affected count in README, RESULTS, METHOD, STATE and HANDOFF, and move the pinned USTB live window to end on 2026-11-24. In METHOD, state that the API returns forward-filled labels for dates without a published NAV, including future dates. Weekend and holiday carries are therefore API fills, not valuation strikes, and the same-date label at 23:59:59 UTC was very likely unpublished at that instant.

gaps.issue: The documented clean-clone path (capture, then replay) reproduced every USTB metric and the exact chart bytes today. It will stop working once Superstate publishes the November 25 NAV, which changes the 11/25 and 11/26 labels. The reference labels_sha256 covers those two forward-filled labels, so any later capture fails replay with 'historical issuer label/value checksum mismatch'. Full inputs are not committed, so no offline route around the capture exists. This is inferred from the forward-fill evidence. It has not been observed yet.
gaps.fix: Apply the official-NAV-date cutoff from the evidence gap so that the pinned digest covers only published NAVs. Add a regression test with a synthetic issuer payload whose trailing filled label is revised after capture. The digest must stay stable and replay must pass.

gaps.issue: The chart title 'USTB trailed Superstate's NAV' needs a footnote to be true and names the fund rather than the feed. What it plots is mostly built in by construction. It compares the feed at 23:59:59 UTC with a same-date label that the issuer most likely had not published yet. The result is two bands, about -1 bp on most weekdays and about -3 bp on Fridays (weekend accrual), and both track the Treasury bill yield. The -5.86 bp extreme on 2024-07-29 combines Friday accrual with the skipped 2024-07-26 value, and nothing on the chart or in RESULTS links the two. The two rightmost points at 0 bp are forward-fill artefacts. In the 1360 px render, the '-5.86' label overlaps a data point.
gaps.fix: Replace the headline figure with a delivery-schedule chart from the replay. Plot one mark per issuer value from 2024-06-27 to the official NAV date, coded as 'next valuation date' (589), 'one day late' (4) and 'never appeared' (8). Use a title of 20 words or fewer that holds without a footnote, for example '589 of 593 USTB NAV changes reached Chainlink the next valuation day'. Keep the UTC-close series in RESULTS under an exact label (gap to the later-dated issuer label). Remove provisional days, check label collisions at 342 and 680 px, rerun render --check and update the SHA-256 values in post-review.json and HANDOFF.

gaps.issue: Draft 1 repeats the 584 count as 'one NYSE session after', but two of those changes posted on a Saturday. Drafts 2 and 3 report basis-point gaps against dated labels that Superstate very likely published on the same morning as the feed post (Veterans Day 2025: the issuer label carries the November 10 NAV, so the fund did not value on November 11). Readers will take both drafts as oracle staleness, a reading the evidence does not support. Draft 4 is sound.

gaps.issue: The 21 tests are behavioural and cover parser, ABI, multicall, switch, chart and EDGAR failure paths. They miss the logic where this review found defects: the session-count vs posting-date semantics (a Saturday post after one session), forward-filled trailing labels, month-end selection (the 2024-10-31 value posted Saturday 2024-11-02 is counted 'one session later'), coverage and uncovered values, the 23:59:59 sampling boundary, and replay rejecting a labels_sha256 or chain_sha256 mismatch against the reference.
gaps.fix: Add focused tests in tests/test_feed_history.py: a Friday label posted Saturday (1 session, not on the next session date); a Columbus Day carry (2 NYSE sessions, next valuation date); trailing fills after official.nav_date excluded from the digest and the daily rows; a month-end that posts on a weekend; a round at 23:59:59 vs 00:00:00 UTC; and replay with a tampered reference digest exiting 1.

Restate month-end on the posting-date definition (26 of 28 on the next session date, 27 within one session). Point the README at the current quality review.

gaps.issue: The study measures one oracle on one chain. RESULTS states this limit. A measured delivery schedule, a skipped-value incident list and the forward-fill behaviour go beyond NavBridge's simulated data and the vendor's heartbeat parameter. A cross-oracle comparison would be the result most likely to be cited.
gaps.fix: Optional extension: run the same join for one more USTB feed with public history, for example a Chronicle or RedStone USTB feed on Ethereum, or Chainlink USTB on another chain. Report next-valuation-date delivery and skipped values side by side.

gaps.issue: The issuer's publication time is unknown, so date-to-chain time combines the valuation strike, issuer publication and oracle posting. The new forward-fill evidence suggests Superstate publishes on the next valuation morning. If so, the feed's roughly 09:10 ET posting may follow publication within minutes. This is optional and does not lower the score.
gaps.fix: Decide whether to approve a single bounded polling window on one business morning (for example every 5 minutes, 06:00 to 10:00 ET) of the public financials endpoint. The window would record when official.nav_date advances, bracketing publication against that day's onchain round.
